headlines.title: Bay Area airports face lingering flight delays, cancellations Sunday
headlines.description: Residual travel disruptions from Friday’s nationwide ground stoppage continued to impact travelers across the region, with all three Bay Area airports reporting flight cancellations and delays throughout the day. While the Federal Aviation Administration expected fully normal operations to resume, the recovery came a day too late for one South Bay family. Activity at Mineta San Jose International Airport quieted down significantly compared to earlier in the day, but Friday’s ground stop devastated wedding plans for the Bhamidipati family of Milpitas. Many of their family members and friends remain stranded in San Jose or in cities across the country, unable to attend the ceremony. The Bhamidipati family had planned a destination wedding weekend in Austin, Texas, following a traditional Indian ceremony in the South Bay. Instead, they found themselves stranded at the airport alongside thousands of other passengers. “We were all supposed to fly out Friday, but yeah that didn’t happen,” said Sandy Bhamidipati. Sandy, his wife, their son, and her parents tried desperately to book flights for everyone through different airlines and airports. By Saturday afternoon, however, they were only able to secure a single seat. That ticket went to the groom, who will barely make it to his wedding on Sunday. “I’m happy that the groom, at least, was able to fly, but the wedding party, they don’t even know how many people will show up,” Bhamidipati said. According to Flightradar24, which tracks air traffic nationwide, 41 flights were canceled and 180 more were delayed at Mineta San Jose. Conditions were even worse at other airports across the country. As a result, a wedding celebration originally expected to draw more than a hundred guests is now anticipating an attendance of only 20 to 30 people. “His friends, for example. He went to Arizona State, so everybody he knew are from Arizona, or places around. The bride also went to Arizona State, so they have too many friends from that place. They couldn’t fly out. Families couldn’t fly out,” Bhamidipati explained. To compound the frustration, Bhamidipati said he is uncertain whether he will receive refunds for hotel and Airbnb bookings or flight reservations made through a third-party vendor. He noted that American Airlines could not honor those third-party reservations because the carrier lacked available seats. “Same with my brother-in-law. He has like six or seven reservations, everywhere, so he’s probably trying to cancel tickets now,” Bhamidipati said. Between multiple unsuccessful flight arrangements, catering, and Airbnb reservations, the family estimates they could lose tens of thousands of dollars. Some vendors have already informed them that it is too late for refunds. According to FlightAware, as of 9 a.m. Sunday, the three major Bay Area airports were reporting: SFO: 138 delays, 54 cancellations; SJC: 46 delays, 12 cancellations; OAK: 35 delays, eight cancellations. There were reportedly 219 delays and 74 cancellations in the Bay Area. Numbers are as of 9 a.m. Sunday and could change throughout the day, FlightAware stated.

While the Federal Aviation Administration expected fully normal operations to resume, the recovery came a day too late for one South Bay family. Activity at Mineta San Jose International Airport quieted down significantly compared to earlier in the day, but Friday’s ground stop devastated wedding plans for the Bhamidipati family of Milpitas. Many of their family members and friends remain stranded in San Jose or in cities across the country, unable to attend the ceremony. The Bhamidipati family had planned a destination wedding weekend in Austin, Texas, following a traditional Indian ceremony in the South Bay. Instead, they found themselves stranded at the airport alongside thousands of other passengers. “We were all supposed to fly out Friday, but yeah that didn’t happen,” said Sandy Bhamidipati. Sandy, his wife, their son, and her parents tried desperately to book flights for everyone through different airlines and airports. By Saturday afternoon, however, they were only able to secure a single seat. That ticket went to the groom, who will barely make it to his wedding on Sunday. “I’m happy that the groom, at least, was able to fly, but the wedding party, they don’t even know how many people will show up,” Bhamidipati said. According to Flightradar24, which tracks air traffic nationwide, 41 flights were canceled and 180 more were delayed at Mineta San Jose. Conditions were even worse at other airports across the country. As a result, a wedding celebration originally expected to draw more than a hundred guests is now anticipating an attendance of only 20 to 30 people. “His friends, for example. He went to Arizona State, so everybody he knew are from Arizona, or places around. The bride also went to Arizona State, so they have too many friends from that place. They couldn’t fly out. Families couldn’t fly out,” Bhamidipati explained. To compound the frustration, Bhamidipati said he is uncertain whether he will receive refunds for hotel and Airbnb bookings or flight reservations made through a third-party vendor. He noted that American Airlines could not honor those third-party reservations because the carrier lacked available seats. “Same with my brother-in-law. He has like six or seven reservations, everywhere, so he’s probably trying to cancel tickets now,” Bhamidipati said. Between multiple unsuccessful flight arrangements, catering, and Airbnb reservations, the family estimates they could lose tens of thousands of dollars. Some vendors have already informed them that it is too late for refunds. According to FlightAware, as of 9 a.m. Sunday, the three major Bay Area airports were reporting: SFO: 138 delays, 54 cancellations; SJC: 46 delays, 12 cancellations; OAK: 35 delays, eight cancellations. There were reportedly 219 delays and 74 cancellations in the Bay Area. Numbers are as of 9 a.m. Sunday and could change throughout the day, FlightAware stated.
